diagnosis.root_cause: Progressive optical receive-power loss on ONU EPON0/3:14, consistent with degradation in the subscriber fibre path or its connectors/splitter leg. RX power declined from approximately -19.2 dBm to -26.45 dBm over seven days and is currently -27.1 dBm, while TX power, TX bias, distance, voltage, and ONU status remain normal.
evidence: The subscriber ONU is online and responding, so this is not an ONU-offline condition.
Current RX power is -27.1 dBm, in the degraded range and close to the critical threshold of -28 dBm.
Seven-day RX telemetry shows a sustained progressive decline from about -19 dBm to -26.45 dBm, far wider than the healthy +/-0.3 dBm noise floor.
TX power remains around +2.3 dBm and within the normal EPON range, excluding a transmit-power fault.
TX bias current stays near 11 mA and does not rise, providing no evidence of laser ageing.
Distance remains constant at 188 m, excluding a changed fibre route or distance-change fault.
Peers on EPON0/3 have normal optical levels, so the issue is isolated to this subscriber path rather than the PON port or splitter as a whole.
The OLT, PON port, router, VLAN, RADIUS records, and authentication state are healthy and consistent.
The subscriber has 9 sessions in 24 hours, exceeding the flapping threshold and matching an optical-loss symptom, but the session instability is secondary to the fibre degradation.
OLT-wide offline count is at the normal baseline and OLT telemetry is healthy, so there is no OLT-wide outage.
PON traffic data does not establish a port-congestion fault; the strongest objective fault evidence is the progressive optical RX loss.

remediation.action: Open a fibre fault for customer 20418. Inspect and clean/reseat the ONU, drop fibre, connectors, patch panel, and splitter port; perform OTDR and optical power tests, then repair or replace the degraded fibre component. Monitor RX power and session frequency after repair. Do not replace the OLT, router, ONU laser, or alter RADIUS/VLAN configuration unless field testing finds an unrelated issue.

ground_truth.root_cause: Progressive attenuation in the fibre path between the splitter and this customer's ONU, consistent with a bend, damaged connector or degrading splice on the drop.
expected_reasoning: Cached RX of -26.40 dBm sits in the degraded band (-25 to -28)
Telemetry shows RX falling from -19.2 to -26.4 dBm over six days against a +/-0.3 dBm noise floor, so this is a trend and not a spot reading
Live RX of -27.10 is below the cached -26.40, so degradation is still progressing
TX power, TX bias current, supply voltage and distance are all flat, so the ONU laser and the fibre geometry are unchanged
Port neighbours on EPON0/3 read -19 to -22 dBm, so the PON port, feeder and splitter are healthy
The fault is therefore downstream of the splitter, in this customer's own fibre path
Nine sessions in 24h against a 2-3 baseline is a symptom of the marginal link, not an independent auth fault
Declining daily traffic is consistent with intermittent connectivity
distractors: Elevated session count invites a session_flapping_auth diagnosis
Declining traffic alone could suggest congestion
One neighbour (EPON0/3:21) is offline for unrelated reasons, at the 4.85% network baseline
